name: Honjo-Azumabashi
tagline: Tokyo in 17 minutes and Otemachi in 18 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000.
summary: The station is in Sumida City, served by Toei Asakusa Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 18 minutes to Otemachi, 31 minutes to Shinjuku, 37 minutes to Shibuya and 29 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. The station stands 1.2 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 3.4 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 1.2 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 0.7 m to 4.1 m, a difference of 3.4 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 8 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 8 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is about average for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 4 clinics and 10 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 墨田病院, about 12 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 山田記念病院, about 15 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Toei Asakusa Line.
congestion: Toei Asakusa Line runs at 123% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch of the line is 本所吾妻橋→浅草, which includes this station. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥110,000 to ¥120,000 and 1K ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. 1LDK ¥180,000 to ¥190,000 and 2LDK ¥220,000 to ¥230,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. schools and parks within walking distance pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Tokyo-Skytree is ahead on the number of medical facilities, but Honjo-Azumabashi is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Honjo-Azumabashi. Tokyo-Skytree has the Tobu Skytree Line, a different set from Honjo-Azumabashi. To Roppongi, for instance, Tokyo-Skytree takes 6 minutes longer. A one-room flat costs about ¥6,000 less at Tokyo-Skytree. On how little of the area is in the flood projection, Honjo-Azumabashi comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Asakusa is ahead on the number of lines and the number of medical facilities, but Honjo-Azumabashi is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection and quiet.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Honjo-Azumabashi. Asakusa also has the Tobu Skytree Line and Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, which Honjo-Azumabashi does not. With more lines, Asakusa is the better connected of the two. To Shinjuku, for instance, Asakusa is 3 minutes quicker. On what it offers families, though, Honjo-Azumabashi comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 6 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 7 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Toei Asakusa Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
